firing.source:
declare let a: any, b: any;
export function run() { if(1) {} }

findings.message: This condition is always the same value, so the branch it guards either always runs or never does. Nothing reports it: the code compiles, the dead half type-checks, and a reader sees a decision being made where none is. It is usually a comparison that lost an operand, or a guard someone stubbed out and did not restore.

clean.source:
declare let a: any, b: any;
export const value = 1;
